issues.legal_issue: A surviving widow’s land rights became absolute under the later succession laws, requiring her to be recorded as the absolute owner and bhumidar.
material_facts: The widow of the last proprietor was recorded as his widow and had been mutated on the basis of a statement allegedly made before the later succession laws came into force.

When the consolidation authorities decided the dispute, the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act and the Hindu Succession Act had come into force and conferred absolute proprietary rights on the widow.
The widow was still alive when the Supreme Court decided the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The widow was the absolute proprietor of the land and had to be recorded as its absolute owner and bhumidar; the consolidation decision and the High Court judgment were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act and the Hindu Succession Act conferred absolute proprietary rights on the widow, so the earlier statement and the view that she held only a life interest could not govern the decision. No earlier cases were cited.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a consolidation decision concerns a surviving recorded widow and later succession laws granted her absolute property rights, she must be recorded as the absolute landowner.

issues.legal_issue: Collateral reversioners have no standing to challenge a surviving widow’s status once later succession laws have made her the absolute owner.
material_facts: The respondents claimed an interest in the land as the widow’s collaterals and contended that she had only a life interest.
The widow was still alive, and the later succession laws had conferred absolute proprietary rights on her.
The consolidation authority accepted the collaterals’ claim and treated the widow as holding only a life interest.
issues.conclusion: The collaterals’ interest ceased when the widow became the absolute owner, and they had no locus to challenge her status.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that once the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act and the Hindu Succession Act conferred absolute ownership on the widow, the collaterals’ reversionary interest ceased and they had no locus to challenge her status. No earlier cases were cited.

issues.definition: When a surviving widow is the absolute owner and claimants assert only a collateral reversionary interest, those claimants have no standing to challenge her status.
